To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inhibition of gap‐junctional intercellular communication in astrocytes leads to an increase in glucose metabolism that is associated with an up‐regulation in glucose transporters and in type I and II hexokinases.
gap junctions are involved in the regulation of glucose uptake and proliferation of astrocytes.

(1) gap junctions control glucose metabolism and proliferation in normal and transformed astrocytes; (2) cyclins D1, and to a lesser extent D3, act as sensors of gap junctional inhibition and as mediators of the mitogenic response in astrocytes; and (3) gap junctions are involved in the regulation of the proliferative status in astrocytes by modulating glucose metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the role of gap junctions in brain physiology and pathology, with a special focus on their implication in the regulation of glucose metabolism and in the control of proliferation in glial cells.
the study of the role of gap junctional intercellular communication in astrocytes and glioma cells, and its impact on their glucose metabolism and proliferation.
the identification of the molecular pathways involved in the control of proliferation of glioma and normal astrocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gap junctions play a role in the control of the metabolic and proliferative status of astrocytes and that this control could be a key element in glioma cell behavior.
gap junctions are not only involved in the control of cell proliferation but also in metabolic control.
the inhibition of gap‐junctional communication induces a metabolic shift that favors the proliferative activity of astrocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inhibition of gap function communication in astrocytes induces the expression and/or the activity of cyclins D1, D3 and hexokinase, and this in turn increases glucose uptake and proliferation.
the modulation of gap junctions in glia affects glucose metabolism and proliferation, and this effect could be used to control the proliferation of gliomas.
astrocytic gap‐junctional communication is a key element in glucose uptake and proliferation in glial cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gap junctions play a crucial role in the control of the proliferation of gliomas and that their inhibition is an important factor in the increased glucose uptake observed in these tumors.
the inhibition of astrocytic communication leads to a rapid change of the metabolic state of the cells.
the modulation of gap junctional intercellular communication is a powerful way to control the proliferation of gliomas.
